assessments.reasoning: The pinned OpenLDAP project file names Howard Y.H. Chu, Symas Corporation, Hallvard B. Furuseth, Gavin Henry and Suretec Systems Ltd. in a distinct contributor block. The Foundation, Zeilenga/Net Boolean/IBM and University of Michigan material falls outside that block. The full-file SHA-256 independently matched the claim and the decision row. Capture 346395f1351341d587d1482ad1782e90. [OpenLDAP COPYRIGHT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openldap/openldap/b9c1d8f93d7a532b6b17a32b52dfc14530e139f7/COPYRIGHT)

The pinned Index decision ties the active row to the matching entity, edition, full-file digest, OpenLDAP commit and contributor-block boundaries. The decision describes Index maintenance and makes the classification applicable after qualification. Capture b5ea5cec924542bbbe9fd18c42a8cc50. [Index lifecycle decision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/software-commons/license-index/d4f01348ddb8d64db53ffdea82f5706d5e73af24/docs/decisions/openldap-imapsync-notices-classification.md)

limitations: Scope is limited to the specified contributor notice and the Index's lifecycle assignment. Separate notices, project-wide applicability, reuse and installation require separate evidence.

The adoption bundle digest was verified as a manifest declaration. The CI caller's two pins were verified against the policy commit. Bundle reconstruction, execution-record export and publication qualification were outside this review.
reasoning: The publisher establishes the notice's identity and the Index decision establishes its assigned lifecycle. Checking adjacent notices and matching the decision's commit and full-file digest tests whether the assignment accidentally covers a different notice.
